matches.rationale: No finding addresses the suspicious implausible metrics or selective reporting in Table 1; the data integrity findings concern copy/paste errors in Table 2 (pred6) and inconsistency between Tables 1 and 2 (pred7), not the fabricated performance jumps described in GT1.

Finding pred2 identifies a density factor inconsistency but states the paper multiplies by √ρ and that large ρ increases similarity, whereas the GT corruption is division by √ρ under a different assumption. The specific mathematical operation and logical flaw described are not the same.
No finding mentions missing hyperparameter/implementation details (learning rates, batch sizes, epochs) or the experimental protocol asymmetry that makes gains unverifiable.

Both GT4 and pred1 identify the same scientific issue: the Abstract overclaims retrieval performance relative to the actual low R@1 scores (below 40%) and the Limitations section's admission of relatively low performance.
No finding challenges the citation of [44] (Palmer & Faloutsos 2000) as a data mining sampling paper not supporting the claimed Bayesian correction theory.
No finding mentions the absence of ethical/IRB statements, informed consent, or privacy considerations for using real-world ScanNet indoor scans.
No finding addresses the inflated marketing-style phrasing ('break through the bottleneck') in the Introduction that exaggerates the contribution relative to incremental empirical gains.

No finding identifies the notational inconsistency where multiple text representations (u_i, ū_i, s_i) in Equation (5) are never clearly related to the original query t_i or the interactive dialogue context D_i.

No finding points out the selective reporting in Table 3 that omits ablations for critical hyperparameters (number of rounds, temperature τ, constant ε) despite Figure 4 showing sensitivity to these choices.

No finding discusses the contradiction where boundary features are claimed to be noisy and aggregated at the hypersphere center, while standard SVDD treats boundary points as the most informative support vectors.
No finding raises the information leakage concern that fine-grained memory may include descriptions of the ground-truth target scene, making comparisons with baselines unfair.
No finding calls out the downplaying of clear performance degradation after peak interaction rounds (coarse-grained drops after round 3) as merely 'slight' degradation in Section 4.5.

No finding notes the inflated novelty claim around applying Chain-of-Thought prompting (citation [47]) as a methodological contribution when it is a straightforward application yielding minimal ablation gain.
No finding discusses the omitted dual-use/misuse risks (automated surveillance, unauthorized spatial profiling) in the Limitations and Potential Impact Statement.
No finding describes the misalignment where the abstract frames IAT as online domain adaptation during interaction, but Section 3.3 reveals it is a separate pre-deployment tuning phase.
